integrations.title: Next.js
integrations.summary: Runs the editor in a client component that loads without server rendering.
integrations.checked: Tested with Next.js 16.4, React 19.3 and Froala 5.5.0 in Chrome.
integrations.markdown:
# Froala with Next.js

Next.js renders client components on the server once, and Froala needs the browser. Importing it in a `'use client'` file is not enough, because `next build` then fails with `ReferenceError: Element is not defined`.

## Set it up

Call `froala_get_setup` with target `nextjs`. It gives four files in `app/froala/`.

| File                  | What it does                                               |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `froala-enhancements` | Adds safe pasting, keyboard access and screen reader names |
| `froala-preset`       | Holds the plugins, the CSS and the settings                |
| `FroalaEditorClient`  | The client component that renders the editor               |
| `FroalaEditor`        | Loads `FroalaEditorClient` with `ssr: false`               |

Import `FroalaEditor`, never `FroalaEditorClient`, in your pages.

```tsx
import FroalaEditor from './froala/FroalaEditor';

export default function Page() {
  return <FroalaEditor />;
}
```

## The rules that keep the build working

- Keep every import of `froala-editor` and `react-froala-wysiwyg` in files that only `FroalaEditorClient` reaches.
- Call `dynamic()` with `ssr: false` in a file that starts with `'use client'`. Next.js rejects it in a Server Component.
- Set your licence key in `NEXT_PUBLIC_FROALA_KEY`. The preset uses the public trial key until you do.

## Tailwind CSS

`create-next-app` adds Tailwind by default, and its preflight removes list bullets and heading sizes in the editor. `froala_get_setup` adds `froala-content.css` when package.json lists `tailwindcss`.

## Pages Router

Put the folder in `components/`. `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false` works the same way.

integrations.title: Nuxt
integrations.summary: Registers the wrapper in a client-only plugin and keeps the editor out of server rendering.
integrations.checked: Tested with Nuxt 4.6, Vue 3.5 and Froala 5.5.0 in Chrome.
integrations.markdown:
# Froala with Nuxt

Nuxt renders pages on the server, and Froala needs the browser. Everything that loads Froala goes in a plugin that ends in `.client`, and the component wraps the editor in `<ClientOnly>`.

## Set it up

Call `froala_get_setup` with target `nuxt`. It gives these files.

| File                              | What it does                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app/froala/froala-enhancements`  | Adds safe pasting, keyboard access and screen reader names                 |
| `app/froala/froala-config`        | Holds the settings, with no Froala import, so the server can read it       |
| `app/plugins/froala.client`       | Loads Froala, its plugins and CSS in the browser, and registers `<froala>` |
| `app/components/FroalaEditor.vue` | Renders the editor inside `<ClientOnly>`                                   |

Nuxt imports components for you, so use `<FroalaEditor />` in any page.

## The licence key

The preset uses the public trial key until you set your own. Add the key to the runtime config, and set `NUXT_PUBLIC_FROALA_KEY` in `.env`.

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  runtimeConfig: { public: { froalaKey: '' } }
});
```

## Nuxt 4.5 and newer

These versions use Vite 8. With Froala 5.5.0 or older, the build passes and the page shows an inert `<froala>` element. Froala 5.6.0 fixes this, so upgrade both Froala packages together.

## Nuxt 3

Nuxt 3 keeps `plugins` and `components` at the top level. `froala_get_setup` follows the version in package.json.

integrations.title: Svelte and SvelteKit
integrations.summary: Uses the Svelte wrapper, and turns off server rendering for the route that shows the editor.
integrations.checked: Tested with Svelte 5.57, SvelteKit 3.1 and Froala 5.5.0 in Chrome.
integrations.markdown:
# Froala with Svelte

The `svelte-froala-wysiwyg` wrapper needs Svelte 5.

## Set it up

Call `froala_get_setup` with target `svelte`. It gives these files in `src/lib/froala/`.

| File                  | What it does                                               |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `froala-enhancements` | Adds safe pasting, keyboard access and screen reader names |
| `froala-preset`       | Holds the plugins, the CSS and the settings                |
| `FroalaEditor.svelte` | Renders the editor                                         |

In a TypeScript project it also adds `src/froala.d.ts`, because the wrapper ships without types.

## SvelteKit

SvelteKit renders pages on the server, and Froala needs the browser. Turn server rendering off for the route that shows the editor, in its `+page.ts` or `+layout.ts`.

```ts
export const ssr = false;
```

SvelteKit 3 renamed the `$lib` alias to `#lib`.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import FroalaEditor from '#lib/froala/FroalaEditor.svelte';
</script>

<FroalaEditor />
```

## The licence key

Set your licence key as `VITE_FROALA_KEY` in `.env`. The preset uses the public trial key until you do.
